01

Setting specification

Task

Find an approximate second-order stationary point of the full objective:

$$\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2\le\varepsilon_g,\qquad\nabla^2f(\widehat{x})\succeq-\varepsilon_H I_d.$$

Admissible model

The objective $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ is $C^k$ and bounded below; nonconvexity is allowed.

The objective has a finite infimum, and the public initial point $x_0$ satisfies $f(x_0)-\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x)\le\Delta$.

$$\|D^{k}f(x)-D^{k}f(y)\|_{\mathrm{op},2}\le M_k\|x-y\|_{2}.$$

Fix $k\ge2$; no additional lower-order regularity bound is imposed.

Admissible parameter domain: $$d\ge1,\quad k\ge2;\quad\text{all other parameters satisfy their tabulated ranges}.$$

Oracle interface

Each query selects $x$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and returns the complete exact tuple $J_{k}f(x)=(f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^{k}f(x))$. The fixed objective uniquely determines the response, with no stochastic noise.

The public inputs are $x_0$, the target accuracy, and $d$, $k$, $\Delta$, $M_k$, $\varepsilon_g$, $\varepsilon_H$. Numerical constants are admissible bounds and need not equal the sharp constants of the instance. The objective, unqueried derivatives, minimizer and minimum value are hidden.

Output

Return $\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^d$.

The output may be an unqueried point, a feasible average of past iterates, or another feasible postprocessing result. No function value or additional computable certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

Scale the gradient norm and the negative-curvature residual by their respective tolerances. The base error is the larger scaled residual, so a value at most one means that both tolerances are met.

The base error is

$$\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})=\max\left\{\frac{\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2}{\varepsilon_g},\frac{[-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(\widehat{x}))]_+}{\varepsilon_H}\right\}.$$

$[a]_+=\max\{a,0\}$, and $\lambda_{\min}$ denotes the smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix. The target is $\mathcal{E}(\widehat{x})\le1$, where $\varepsilon_g$ and $\varepsilon_H$ are independent positive tolerances.

Resource accounting

Each primitive response specified under ORACLE costs one unit. Queries at new points introduced by any inner procedure also count toward the total.

The resource budget is a fixed worst-case cap on every execution path. Initialization, stopping checks, and all actual responses in a batch are included.

Arithmetic, linear algebra, tensor operations, storage, and global solution of known models are free. Bit complexity, communication, and wall-clock time are not counted.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Deterministic

Arbitrary measurable adaptive deterministic algorithms are allowed.

No linear-span, Krylov or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Memory and internal computation are unrestricted.

Information is acquired adaptively in query order. Parallel submission does not reduce the number of actual responses counted. There is no communication-round or memory budget. Exact real arithmetic and arbitrarily small positive query separations are allowed.

Choose one algorithm from the public inputs, then require its guarantee separately for every admissible instance and oracle law.

$$\max\left\{\frac{\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2}{\varepsilon_g},\frac{[-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(\widehat{x}))]_+}{\varepsilon_H}\right\}\le 1.$$

The running-cost guarantee is specified separately under RESOURCE.

Randomized

Arbitrary measurable adaptive algorithms with private randomness are allowed.

No linear-span, Krylov or zero-respecting restriction is imposed. Memory and internal computation are unrestricted.

Information is acquired adaptively in query order. Parallel submission does not reduce the number of actual responses counted. There is no communication-round or memory budget. Exact real arithmetic and arbitrarily small positive query separations are allowed.

Choose one algorithm from the public inputs, then require its guarantee separately for every admissible instance and oracle law.

$$\Pr\!\left[\max\left\{\frac{\|\nabla f(\widehat{x})\|_2}{\varepsilon_g},\frac{[-\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(\widehat{x}))]_+}{\varepsilon_H}\right\}\le 1\right]\ge\frac23.$$

Expectation or probability is evaluated after fixing the instance; randomness comes from the algorithm's private random seed.

The running-cost guarantee is specified separately under RESOURCE.

02

Notation and parameters

$x,\widehat{x},x_0$

Query or decision point, algorithm output, and public initial point.

Domain
$\mathbb{R}^d$
$\mathbb{R}^d$

Real coordinate space; vectors use the Euclidean norm unless otherwise stated.

Domain
$d$ is a positive integer.
$\langle u,v\rangle,\ \|u\|_2$

Euclidean inner product and norm.

$$\langle u,v\rangle=u^\top v,\qquad\|u\|_2=\sqrt{\langle u,u\rangle}.$$

$D^jf(x),\ \nabla f(x),\ \nabla^2f(x)$

Fréchet derivative of order $j$, gradient and Hessian.

Domain
$j\in\{0,\ldots,k\}$ and $D^0f=f$.
$\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}},\ \|T\|_{\mathrm{op},2}$

Induced operator norm of a Euclidean multilinear tensor; the spectral norm for matrices.

$$\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{op},2}=\sup_{\|u_1\|_2,\ldots,\|u_j\|_2\le1}|T[u_1,\ldots,u_j]|.$$

$\mathcal{E}$

Base error defined in the metric specification; expectation or probability aggregation is imposed by the guarantee.

$N$

Total number of original oracle calls; the unit cost is specified in the resource convention.

Domain
$N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$.
$T^*$

Minimum worst-case budget for one algorithm to meet the requirement on the full instance class, within the specified regime, guarantee and resource projection. Expected-resource specifications instead minimize the per-instance expected budget.

$O,\Omega,\Theta,\widetilde{O}$

Asymptotic upper bounds, lower bounds, matching bounds up to constants, and upper bounds omitting the declared logarithmic factors.

Domain
Hidden constants, fixed parameters, and omitted logarithmic variables are specified for each bound.
$\inf,\sup,\min,\max$

Infimum, supremum, attained minimum and attained maximum.

$c,C$

Positive universal constants without assigned numerical values; a subscript permits dependence only on the indicated fixed parameters.

Domain
$0<c,C<\infty$.
$J_{k}f(x)$

Function value and the complete tuple of derivatives from order one through the specified maximum order.

$$J_{k}f(x)=(f(x),Df(x),\ldots,D^{k}f(x)).$$

$f,f^*$

Unknown objective and its global infimum over the specified feasible domain.

$$f^*=\inf_{x\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(x).$$

$\lambda_{\min}(A),[z]_+$

The smallest eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix and the positive part of a scalar.

$$[z]_+=\max\{z,0\}.$$

$I_d$

The identity matrix in dimension $d$.

$d$

Ambient dimension; dimension requirements are stated separately for each bound.

Domain
$d\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge1}$
$k$

Maximum order of the query interface and Taylor model; this integer is fixed before other parameters are compared.

Domain
$k\in\mathbb{N}_{\ge2}$
$\Delta$

Upper bound on the difference between the objective value at the known initial point and its global infimum.

Domain
$\Delta\ge0$
$M_k$

Global Lipschitz upper bound for the order-$k$ derivative in the tensor operator norm.

Domain
$M_k\ge0$
$\varepsilon_g$

Gradient-norm tolerance

Domain
$\varepsilon_g>0$
$\varepsilon_H$

Tolerance for negative Hessian curvature

Domain
$\varepsilon_H>0$
$C_k$

A sufficiently large positive constant depending only on the fixed order $k$, without a numerical value specified.

Domain
$C_k>0$
$A$

Gradient workload

Domain
$A\ge0$

$$A=\Delta\,(M_k)^{\frac{1}{k}}\,((\varepsilon_g)^{(-1)\,(\frac{k+1}{k})}).$$

$B$

Negative-curvature workload

Domain
$B\ge0$

$$B=\Delta\,((M_k)^{\frac{2}{k-(1)}})\,((\varepsilon_H)^{(-1)\,(\frac{k+1}{k-(1)})}).$$

$C_0$

Fixed gradient-dominance ratio in this regime, retained as a symbolic constant.

Domain
$C_0>0$
$\mathbb{E},\Pr$

Expectation and probability after fixing the instance; their randomness sources are specified by the guarantee.

/proofs/0/body · SHA-256 8b2356c60fae01a303ef034de840ae671bb7c46284ad3aff7534fc86c1242ca8
The noiseless specialization in ACDFSS20, Appendix H.2, gives a zero-respecting curvature lower bound $$\Omega_k\left(\frac\Delta{\varepsilon_H}\min_{2\le j\le k}(M_j/\varepsilon_H)^{2/(j-1)}\right),$$ within the nonautomatic window $\varepsilon_H\le c_kM_1$. For deterministic algorithms, adaptively rotate the smooth gated chain. Unactivated gates have every derivative zero, so each complete jet reveals at most the next direction, including its value response. Choose later directions orthogonal to prior queries and, at the end, to the unqueried output. A sufficient dimension $C_k(1+N)$ accommodates all constraints. Determinism ensures that the final single rotated instance produces the constructed transcript. This seed-dependent adversary argument does not prove an arbitrary-randomized lower bound. With only $M_k$ controlled, choose width $b\asymp(\varepsilon_H/M_k)^{1/(k-1)}$ and amplitude $a\asymp\varepsilon_Hb^2$. Then $$N\asymp_k\Delta M_k^{2/(k-1)}\varepsilon_H^{-(k+1)/(k-1)}.$$ Additional $\beta$-smoothness requires $\varepsilon_H\le c\beta$. Combine this hard family with the separate gradient hard family by taking their maximum, which is equivalent up to a factor two to the sum; no one instance is claimed to realize both difficulties simultaneously. For arbitrary randomized exact second-order algorithms, REUSE26v2's deterministic-loss subclass supplies the separate curvature result. Its gated chain has $O(N)$ value range and dimension-independent Hessian and third-derivative operator bounds. With $\gamma=\varepsilon_H$, spatial scale of order $\gamma$, and amplitude of order $\gamma^3$, take N of order $\gamma^{-3}$. A radial cutoff and wall at radius of order $\gamma^{-1}$ prevent unrestricted distant queries or outputs from bypassing the chain: outside the hard region the gradient is too large, while the transition region retains negative curvature. Conditional exposure of hidden rotation directions and concentration over every query and the final output give the sufficient dimension $$d\ge C_\theta[1+\gamma^{-4}\log(2+\gamma^{-1})+\gamma^{-3}],\qquad\theta=(\beta,M_2,\Delta).$$ Thus, for fixed positive $\theta$ and sufficiently small independent tolerances, the primary result yields $\Omega_{\theta}(\varepsilon_H^{-3})$. Combining it with the randomized gradient lower bound gives the linked exact-J2 bracket. Constants may depend on fixed $\theta$; this is not a joint-parameter lower bound with universal constants, nor a higher-order randomized theorem.

/proofs/1/body · SHA-256 1c686da3222c80218c67595c44cd00127d21854cd62def011f9cb155c68b8246
For each fixed j, use the jth-order regularized method, reading only the relevant part of the complete k-jet. Its budget is $C_j[1+\Delta M_j^{1/j}\varepsilon_g^{-(j+1)/j}]$. All parameters are public, so an algorithm may select the smallest proved budget. This minimum is an envelope of complete algorithms. For the lower bound, use the robust CDHS smooth chain $h_N$, whose initial gap is at most $C_kN$, whose gradient stays bounded away from zero before completion, and whose jth-derivative Lipschitz modulus is at most a constant $\ell_j$ depending only on j. Set $f(x)=a h_N(x/b)$ with $$a/b=K_k\varepsilon_g,\qquad b=\max_{1\le j\le k}(K_k\ell_j\varepsilon_g/M_j)^{1/j}.$$ Then $\operatorname{Lip}(D^jf)=a\ell_j/b^{j+1}\le M_j$ for every j simultaneously. Choosing N proportional to $\Delta/a$ gives N of order A. For A above a fixed k-dependent threshold, deterministic resisting rotations fit in $d\ge C_k(1+A)$; the classical randomized radial construction fits in $d\ge C_k(1+A)^2\log(3+A)$. These are sufficient dimensions. If the primary result is stated as time to query a successful point, append one complete-jet query at the algorithm's final output. A lower bound of N then gives an original-budget lower bound N-1, of the same order in the nontrivial A region. This handles arbitrary unqueried outputs without changing the success quantifier. For $k=2$, the common scaling gives $A=\Delta\min\{\beta\varepsilon_g^{-2},\sqrt{M_2}\varepsilon_g^{-3/2}\}$. Keep the zero-query region $\varepsilon_g^2\ge2\beta\Delta$ separate; the whole domain is not uniformly Theta(1+A). Dimension improvements proved for a highest-order-only model do not automatically preserve all lower-order budgets.

/proofs/2/body · SHA-256 5936b194a7c7301cb3c75257948fbde504be4f0a3e4484ce0992e45f43d47486
At x, form $m_x(s)=T_k(f;x,s)+a_kM_k\|s\|^{k+1}$, choosing $a_k$ sufficiently large, depending only on k, to dominate the Taylor remainder with slack. For $M_k>0$ the model is coercive, so it has a global minimizer, available under the declared free internal computation. Comparing the model at s and zero and applying the value remainder gives $$f(x)-f(x+s)\ge c_kM_k\|s\|^{k+1}.$$ Model first-order optimality and the gradient remainder give $$\|\nabla f(x+s)\|\le C_kM_k\|s\|^k.$$ If the next point is not $\varepsilon_g$-stationary, the decrease is at least $c_kM_k^{-1/k}\varepsilon_g^{(k+1)/k}$. The total decrease is at most $\Delta$, so after the displayed number of calls, including initialization and final verification, stationarity is reached. This is the parameter restoration of the regularized-model argument in BGMST17, Lemmas 2.1–2.3 and Theorem 2.5. Its normalization is $(k-1)!L=M_k$. Separate function and derivative evaluations in the source cost only a fixed multiple when complete jets are charged as one. The argument is about information calls and does not assert an inexpensive arithmetic implementation of global nonconvex model minimization.

Applies only to the indicated objective-gap, first-order, or spectral second-order criteria. A true minimizer need not satisfy a finite-radius high-order Taylor-decrease criterion; those criteria require their own argument. body
/proofs/3/body · SHA-256 b8837d30d87467eb5722fd001e1a97c4b20caf0f43e28cf131ec6217446632ed
For a full-space differentiable objective with $f(x_0)-\inf f\le\Delta$, the condition $\Delta=0$ makes $x_0$ a global minimizer. Its gradient is zero, and its Hessian is positive semidefinite whenever it exists. Thus first-order and spectral second-order stationarity require no query. An objective-gap target also requires no query when $\varepsilon_f\ge\Delta$. Nonnegative query cost proves exact optimality of these zero bounds. If a public gradient-Lipschitz bound $\beta$ is part of the specification, the descent lemma gives $\|\nabla f(x_0)\|^2\le2\beta\Delta$. For convex full-space objectives with a minimizer within distance $R$, it also gives $f(x_0)-f^*\le\beta R^2/2$ and $\|\nabla f(x_0)\|\le\beta R$. These sufficient zero-query regions require that explicit first-order regularity assumption. If only the highest derivative is controlled, positive quadratics can have arbitrary curvature and arbitrarily large initial gap despite zero highest-order modulus. On a connected Euclidean domain, $M_k=0$ or $M_{k,\nu}=0$ makes $D^kf$ constant, so $f$ is a polynomial of degree at most $k$. One complete jet determines all coefficients. Under the specified free internal computation, a known polynomial can then be optimized on a compact public domain, or combined with a public regularizer and solved through the declared known-model interface. A bounded-below polynomial on the full space need not attain its infimum. For approximate spectral stationarity, shift $x_0$ to zero and minimize $f(x)+\eta\|x\|^2/2$. This function is coercive, and its minimizer $x_\eta$ satisfies $\eta\|x_\eta\|^2/2\le\Delta$, $\|\nabla f(x_\eta)\|\le\sqrt{2\eta\Delta}$, and $\nabla^2f(x_\eta)\succeq-\eta I$. Choosing $\eta\le\min\{\varepsilon_H,\varepsilon_g^2/(2\Delta)\}$ meets both targets. For global objective accuracy, exact polynomial coefficients permit arbitrary-accuracy internal global optimization; no additional unknown-function query is needed. To exclude zero queries in a nontrivial region, choose two positive quadratics centered on opposite sides of $x_0$, with the same public budgets and disjoint acceptable-output sets. A zero-query algorithm has the same output distribution on both instances, so their success probabilities sum to at most one. It cannot succeed with probability at least $2/3$ on each. With only highest-order regularity, curvature can be increased until the acceptable sets are disjoint at any prescribed positive accuracy and positive localization radius. In an initial-gap model with additional curvature restrictions, retain the bound's explicit accuracy and compatibility window. If both a global PL constant $\mu$ and a gradient-Lipschitz upper bound $\beta$ are supplied, then $2\mu(f-f_*)\le\|\nabla f\|^2\le2\beta(f-f_*)$. When $\mu>\beta>0$, every gap is zero and the class contains only constant objectives. This degeneracy does not apply without the extra $\beta$ assumption.

/proofs/4/body · SHA-256 c468f489d8a18730cc60d9ab76ba6e3989730b76851602ec483aef92c4068cc5
Retain the frozen full-space C^k, bounded-below objective, gap, jet, output and free-known-model contracts and HO_ENDPOINTS. M_k=0 makes D^k f constant, so the Taylor polynomial of degree at most k recovered from J_k f(x0) equals f everywhere. After this single query set eta=min(epsilon_H,epsilon_g^2/(2Delta))>0 and globally minimize the known coercive polynomial f(x)+eta||x-x0||^2/2 using the permitted free model solution. At a minimizer y, eta||y-x0||^2/2<=f(x0)-inf f<=Delta; therefore ||grad f(y)||=eta||y-x0||<=sqrt(2eta Delta)<=epsilon_g and Hess f(y)>=-eta I>=-epsilon_H I. No further oracle check is required and y may be unqueried. This does not assume that f attains its own infimum. For the lower bound fix lambda>epsilon_g^2/(2Delta), a=sqrt(2Delta/lambda), and f_+(x)=lambda||x-x0-a e1||^2/2, f_-(x)=lambda||x-x0+a e1||^2/2. Both have gap Delta and Lipschitz D^k modulus zero for every k>=2. Their Hessians are positive definite; their acceptable outputs are disjoint balls of radius epsilon_g/lambda because a>epsilon_g/lambda. A zero-query output law is the same on both instances, so its two success probabilities sum to at most one. It cannot give probability >=2/3 on each; the deterministic case follows as well. Integer query counts give cost>=1. Thus the upper and lower costs are exactly one, uniformly in dimension and both tolerances. At Delta=0 the retained zero-query branch applies instead.

/proofs/5/body · SHA-256 bf06092984d730b5ba831094724d3e45d3cc70f1440f410c924483c91663ebae
Read arXiv:2609.28202v2, Definition 3.1 and Theorems 3.2 and 3.4, PDF pp.5-6, archived characters 13323-16400, source SHA256 5129c1f6b8ae94f321c0541890578a5ef396ec08583340160ed877699bae11f9. Set n=1, p=k, L_p=M_k, epsilon=epsilon_g. Then the complete component p-jet is precisely one target complete jet and S_p=1+A. The source class is bounded below with initial gap at most Delta and Lipschitz D^k bound M_k, with no lower-order regularity budget. Any algorithm meeting the target simultaneous gradient/Hessian condition with probability at least 2/3 also meets its gradient condition with that probability, for every positive epsilon_H. The source lower bound is therefore necessary for the target. Theorem 3.4 supplies hard dimension at most C_k(1+A)log(3+A); choose the k-only source constant sufficiently large. For an ambient dimension above this value, pad a hard function h(z) by f(z,w)=h(z). Projection of every query gives an exact equal-cost source query; all derivatives involving dummy coordinates vanish and the remaining complete jet agrees with h. Project the arbitrary output as well. Gap, lower boundedness, tensor operator Lipschitz bound, fixed-path cost and success probability are preserved. Hence an ambient target algorithm below c_k(1+A) would contradict the source theorem. We adopt the conservative A>=C_k subregion. No relation between B and A is used. This is a new q2 bound, not a relabeling or merger of the old q1 bound.

/proofs/7/body · SHA-256 cd6be459c95a7cb052c0e6513e22d459259cb21cc81482807bce2577baff285e
This proof is specifically for the unchanged randomized q2/g1 complete-k-jet scalar-cost contract. Retain the exact existing b1 upper C_k(1+A+B): its quantity_refs explicitly include q2 and it was already adopted in q2 c2/c4. Thus it is an upper for one actual complete algorithm controlling BOTH gradient and Hessian at the SAME output, not an upper obtained by merging q1 and q2 labels or combining algorithms. All initialization, next-point checks and actual full-jet responses are included in its original fixed-path cap; global known-model computations remain free only as allowed by the unchanged model. The independent source-based b5 lower is already a native q2 statement. HO_RANDOMIZED_GRADIENT_TRANSFER uses source Definition3.1/Theorems3.2/3.4 with n1,p=k,Lp=M_k,epsilon=epsilon_g: an algorithm meeting simultaneous gradient/Hessian accuracy with probability>=2/3 necessarily meets gradient accuracy with that probability, for everyepsilon_H>0. The source hard class obeys the same bounded-below initialgap and Lipschitz D^k budget, without adding lower-order regularity. For its harddimension d0<=C_k(1+A)log(3+A), pad h by f(z,w)=h(z). Each arbitrary adaptive target query projects to exactly one source completejet query; dummy derivatives vanish, the remaining tensors agree, and their operator-norm Lipschitz bound and initialgap are unchanged. Project the final arbitrary/unqueried output; targetsuccess implies sourcegradient success. Private randomness, fixedpathcap and per-instance successquantifier are preserved, so every targetalgorithm has cap>=c_k(1+A) on G={Delta>0,M_k>0,A>=C_k,d>=C_k(1+A)log(3+A)}. This is the recorded conservative source guard, including all k-only workload/dimension constants; no lower beyond G is adopted. Now restrict to J=G intersect{B<=C0*A}, with fixed k>=2 and a fixed finite public window constant C0>0 chosen independently of the five native joint parameters. Since 1+A+B<=1+(1+C0)A<=(1+C0)(1+A), the exact q2 envelope obeys c_k(1+A)<=q2*<=C_k(1+C0)(1+A). Hence Theta_{k,C0}(1+A) on J, with a constant ratio independent of d,Delta,M_k,epsilon_g,epsilon_H. C0 is solely a comparison-window constant: it is not an objective smoothness budget, is not substituted by the varying valueB/A, and its dependence is explicitly declared at this comparison. q2's global quantity metadata remains unchanged; this regional result does not assert globally uniform C0-independent optimality. Both B=C0*A and A=C_k are included subject to the sufficiently-large sourceconstant. Positive Delta,M_k and sufficientdimension remain mandatory; zero-gap and polynomial branches are separate. Outside J, especially when B/A grows or outside G, the old q2 comparisons remain unclosed. The old optimal q1 c1 is a distinct registered quantity and is not the publication certificate for q2. This is native publication of the matching consequence already stated in F_RANDOMIZED_GRADIENT and the old boundary ledger, not a new paper lower bound, a new algorithm, or a new blind discovery. No fresh source verification or prior read/approval credit is claimed by this curator proof.

The old zero-gap predicates require Delta=0; the broad old positive branches require M_k>0; the old deterministic large-workload and randomized gradient-dominated windows require max(A,B)>=C_k or A>=C_k with C_k>0; and the residual curvature predicates require k>=3 and B>C0*A, both false here. /joint_analysis/impact/6/argument · SHA-256 cd6be459c95a7cb052c0e6513e22d459259cb21cc81482807bce2577baff285e
This proof is specifically for the unchanged randomized q2/g1 complete-k-jet scalar-cost contract. Retain the exact existing b1 upper C_k(1+A+B): its quantity_refs explicitly include q2 and it was already adopted in q2 c2/c4. Thus it is an upper for one actual complete algorithm controlling BOTH gradient and Hessian at the SAME output, not an upper obtained by merging q1 and q2 labels or combining algorithms. All initialization, next-point checks and actual full-jet responses are included in its original fixed-path cap; global known-model computations remain free only as allowed by the unchanged model. The independent source-based b5 lower is already a native q2 statement. HO_RANDOMIZED_GRADIENT_TRANSFER uses source Definition3.1/Theorems3.2/3.4 with n1,p=k,Lp=M_k,epsilon=epsilon_g: an algorithm meeting simultaneous gradient/Hessian accuracy with probability>=2/3 necessarily meets gradient accuracy with that probability, for everyepsilon_H>0. The source hard class obeys the same bounded-below initialgap and Lipschitz D^k budget, without adding lower-order regularity. For its harddimension d0<=C_k(1+A)log(3+A), pad h by f(z,w)=h(z). Each arbitrary adaptive target query projects to exactly one source completejet query; dummy derivatives vanish, the remaining tensors agree, and their operator-norm Lipschitz bound and initialgap are unchanged. Project the final arbitrary/unqueried output; targetsuccess implies sourcegradient success. Private randomness, fixedpathcap and per-instance successquantifier are preserved, so every targetalgorithm has cap>=c_k(1+A) on G={Delta>0,M_k>0,A>=C_k,d>=C_k(1+A)log(3+A)}. This is the recorded conservative source guard, including all k-only workload/dimension constants; no lower beyond G is adopted. Now restrict to J=G intersect{B<=C0*A}, with fixed k>=2 and a fixed finite public window constant C0>0 chosen independently of the five native joint parameters. Since 1+A+B<=1+(1+C0)A<=(1+C0)(1+A), the exact q2 envelope obeys c_k(1+A)<=q2*<=C_k(1+C0)(1+A). Hence Theta_{k,C0}(1+A) on J, with a constant ratio independent of d,Delta,M_k,epsilon_g,epsilon_H. C0 is solely a comparison-window constant: it is not an objective smoothness budget, is not substituted by the varying valueB/A, and its dependence is explicitly declared at this comparison. q2's global quantity metadata remains unchanged; this regional result does not assert globally uniform C0-independent optimality. Both B=C0*A and A=C_k are included subject to the sufficiently-large sourceconstant. Positive Delta,M_k and sufficientdimension remain mandatory; zero-gap and polynomial branches are separate. Outside J, especially when B/A grows or outside G, the old q2 comparisons remain unclosed. The old optimal q1 c1 is a distinct registered quantity and is not the publication certificate for q2. This is native publication of the matching consequence already stated in F_RANDOMIZED_GRADIENT and the old boundary ledger, not a new paper lower bound, a new algorithm, or a new blind discovery. No fresh source verification or prior read/approval credit is claimed by this curator proof.
